newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran attacks "foreign" role in Afghanistan.
newsitem.headline: Iran attacks "foreign" role in Afghanistan.

text.p: Iran has attacked what it called foreign interference in Afghanistan and said only negotiations among rival factions could restore peace to the ravaged country.

"The Afghan crisis has no military solution...from its very outset Iran has maintained that the crisis could be resolved by the people of that country," the official Iranian news agency IRNA quoted Foreign Ministry spokesman Mahmoud Mohammadi as saying on Sunday night.

Mohammadi said "the interferences into Afghanistan's internal affairs by certain foreign countries cannot solve the problems and those who think that by adopting such policies they can solve the crisis are not only repeating the historical mistakes but also imposing their will on the Afghan people."

Mohammadi did not name the foreign countries, but Iran in the past accused Pakistan of supporting the Taleban movement, which now controls virtually all of Afghanistan after the fall of the northern city of Mazar-i-Shari on Saturday.
Shi'ite Moslem Iran supported the previous Kabul government ousted by the Sunni Taleban, which it accused of giving Islam a bad name by its harsh interpretation of Islamic law.

"Mohammadi said the only way to restore peace in Afghanistan was negotiations between the different groups and formation of a broad-based government comprising all ethnic and political groups of Afghanistan," IRNA said.

The Taleban government appealed for world recognition after its sweeping victories. Pakistan, which has always denied aiding the Taleban, responded immediately and urged other countries and organisations to do the same.
But Iran said it was not ready to recognise the Taleban. President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani said on Sunday Tehran would wait until the United Nations recognised the Taleban government in Kabul.
